summary:
G3 English review of EFMP-302 Unit 4 at commit cf13570, run 003. Independent session; this
reviewer neither drafted nor translated these bytes. All 137 manifest inputs re-hashed and
matched with no missing, extra or changed entry; skill digest matched; git working tree carried
no modification to any bound path before or after the review (log: specs/content/efmp-302/reviews/unit-04/logs-agent-g3-efmp302-u4-run003/manifest-verify.log).

The amended "Unavailable source text" rule (owner ruling D-2026-0001, confirmed) was applied as
written: the three declarations in sources/unit-04.md carry retrieval attempts, the 2026-09-19
date and the owner authorisation, so npst-pakistan-2009, unesco-teacher-ethics and carr2000 no
longer block on unavailability alone. Run-002 findings [1] and [2] are therefore superseded by
the ruling rather than repaired, and are recorded as such. The rubric change closed exactly that
one route and nothing else.

Six of the seven deterministic gates plus check:concept-graph ran clean. The Isore repair that
run 002 found half-propagated is now correct at all seven sites it named, and both figure
geometry defects are gone: fig-U4-4 (viewBox widened 900 -> 940) and fig-U4-8 both measure zero
out-of-bounds text nodes and zero overlapping text boxes in-browser. goe2008 is now cited in
topic-02 and topic-03 prose and in both Further reading lists, and its two relied-on claims are
verbatim-supported by the bound excerpt. RRQ-02 and RRQ-04 mark schemes now match their stems.
All ten MCQ keys were re-derived independently before the key was read and all ten agree.

Disposition is escalate, not pass and not revise. Two blocking content defects survive, one of
them a site of the same Isore defect class that run 002 did not enumerate; and three items
cannot be closed by authoring at all - the Topic 4.4 RRQ shortfall and the four sub-floor
Remember RRQs need an owner decision or a blueprint amendment, the hurst2009 discrepancy needs
the owner to say which record is wrong, and the accreditation claim collides with an escalation
the repository already holds open in specs/gaps.md. This is also the third review cycle on this
submission, past the two-cycle limit the skill sets.

This report is advisory. No qualification record, registry entry or trusted signature exists for
this reviewer identity; nothing here constitutes sign-off, certification or a tracker transition.

findings.message:
Isore repair reached the seven sites run 002 named and missed an eighth of the same class.
docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-04/topic-04.mdx:109-111 reads: "**A misconception this corrects:**
*appraisal and professional development are the same process.* They are related and must be
connected, and they cannot be the same instrument." That is the pre-repair claim, unhedged, in a
box whose format tells the learner it is the corrected truth.
It contradicts three things in the bound inputs:
  (a) the same file twelve lines earlier, topic-04.mdx:94-99: "Be careful how strongly you state
      this ... Isore calls the two purposes \"often conflicting\", and then immediately adds
      \"but not necessarily incompatible\" ... It is not a proof that one document can never do
      both.";
  (b) the bound excerpt specs/content/efmp-302/sources/texts/isore2009.md, para 17 verbatim
      "often conflicting \226 but not necessarily incompatible", para 35 "the Framework can serve
      both summative and formative purposes", Annex 2 s.3 "Conciliating the summative and
      formative purposes in a comprehensive approach";
  (c) the RRQ-04 mark scheme at unit-assessment.mdx:215-216, which instructs the marker: "Do not
      award an answer whose conclusion is that one document cannot hold both".
The practical consequence is the sharpest form of the defect: a candidate who learns the
misconception box and applies it to RRQ-04 is denied a mark by the same document.
REPAIR: bring topic-04.mdx:111 to the strength the body and the source carry - the two are
conflicting and a combined instrument will be read as summative unless the system decides the
separation in advance - or drop the absolute clause. One-line change; do not weaken :94-99 to
match it instead.
Distinguish from run-002 [0]: that finding listed seven sites and all seven are repaired. This is
a newly located eighth site, not a carried-forward one.

Unsupported claim about the learner's own qualification, asserted seven times, and it collides
with an escalation this repository already holds open.
The unit states that Pakistan's teacher education programmes are accredited against the National
Professional Standards for Teachers:
  docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-04/topic-01.mdx:105-106 "they are the framework this country's
    teacher education is accredited against"
  topic-01.mdx:127 "This is why your own degree is accredited against it."
  topic-01.mdx:197 (topic summary, same claim)
  topic-02.mdx:43-45 "They are the framework against which teacher education programmes in
    Pakistan are accredited, which is why they govern your own degree as well as your later
    practice."
  topic-02.mdx:179 (topic summary, same claim)
  topic-04.mdx:47-49 "Your B.Ed, accredited against the National Professional Standards, is the
    mechanism by which you will be certified."
  unit-assessment.mdx:31 (unit summary, same claim)
Why this fails under the amended rubric rather than being covered by D-2026-0001: the claim is
grounded on npst-pakistan-2009 (coverage/unit-04.md rows U4-03, U4-05), which is declared
unretrievable. The declaration at sources/unit-04.md:40 discloses exactly three things as
corroborated-only - the ten standard names, the three-part division, and the 2009 MoE/UNESCO/USAID
origin - and the Supports column scopes it to "the national framework and its origin". Accredit-
ation status is neither. So prose states more than the declaration supports, which is the failure
mode D-2026-0001 explicitly preserved in its "Limits" clause.
It is not merely undeclared, it is contradicted inside the bundle. specs/content/efmp-302/
content-spec.md:376-379, in Unit 2's resolved-gaps record, states: "The drafting note claimed they
resolve to npst-pakistan-2009 because NACTE publishes no separate code of ethics; that was
inferred from a failed search rather than from a document, and review evidence indicates NACTE
does publish its own accreditation standards. The unsupported sentence is removed from the unit,
and the reference is escalated in specs/gaps.md." specs/gaps.md:81-90 carries that open
escalation. Unit 2 removed the conflation of the NPST with NACTE's accreditation standards; Unit 4
asserts it seven times, including to tell the learner what their own degree is accredited against.
REPAIR/ESCALATION: an author can hedge or remove the claim now, but the correct replacement
depends on the NACTE question already escalated in specs/gaps.md, which that entry says needs
"the curriculum owner or a reviewer with access". This finding should be routed there rather than
guessed at. Do not close it by adding the claim to the Unverifiable-sources declaration: the
declaration records what could not be read, not a licence to assert more.

Blueprint shortfall on Topic 4.4, carried from run-002 [6] and independently re-derived. It needs
an owner decision; no authoring repair closes it cleanly.
specs/content/efmp-302/content-spec.md "## Unit 4" -> "Unit-end assessment blueprint" requires
"RRQs (10): Understand to Analyze; >= 2 per topic". Deriving the per-topic assignment from the
Topic column of specs/content/efmp-302/concepts/unit-04.md gives 4.1:4, 4.2:3, 4.3:2, 4.4:1.
Topic 4.4 carries only RRQ-10 (via CON:EFMP-302-4-16). RRQ-04, whose stem at unit-assessment.mdx:
127-130 is substantively Topic 4.4 material, maps solely to CON:EFMP-302-4-6 "Conflict between
the four uses", a Topic 4.1 concept.
Topic 4.4 covers three sub-topics (U4-10, U4-11, U4-12) and the unit's hardest analytical
content, so the shortfall is not cosmetic.
Either add a second Topic 4.4 RRQ, or record an approved decision that RRQ-04 counts toward 4.4
and remap it in the concept graph. Run 001 recorded this as arguable; runs 002 and 003 both
resolve it against 4.4 on the concept graph as committed.
Separately and in the same criterion: RRQ-01 (:117), RRQ-03 (:124), RRQ-05 (:132) and RRQ-08
(:140) are labelled *(Remember)* and, classified from the thinking actually required rather than
the verb, each is answered by reciting a list the unit prints verbatim. Four of ten RRQs sit below
the blueprint's Understand floor. Raise their demand or record an approved amendment to the
blueprint; do not relabel them without changing what they ask.

cf13570.
specs/content/efmp-302/content-spec.md:624 lists hurst2009 (Hurst, B., & Reding, G., 2009,
Professionalism in teaching) among Unit 4's "Mapped readings", and content-spec.md:72 records it
as a guide-required source tagged for units 1 and 3. It appears nowhere in
specs/content/efmp-302/sources/unit-04.md - neither in the table nor in the "## Unverifiable
sources" list - nowhere in specs/content/efmp-302/coverage/unit-04.md, and nowhere in any Unit 4
page. Either the content spec's mapped-readings line or the unit's source record is wrong.
This review cannot tell which was intended; the book is print-only and unreadable from this host,
so even resolving the record would not produce a verified citation. Note that the D-2026-0001
declaration route was applied to carr2000 in this unit but not to hurst2009, which is what makes
the omission look like an oversight rather than a decision.
OWNER DECISION NEEDED: strike hurst2009 from Unit 4's mapped readings, or add it to
sources/unit-04.md with a declaration and a coverage row.

Narrow-viewport figure affordance - a defect I could not settle, and a correction to the run-002
record rather than a repeat of it.
Measured at 360 CSS px (viewport 360x740, dsf 2, isMobile, Chromium 149.0.7827.0; log
specs/content/efmp-302/reviews/unit-04/logs-agent-g3-efmp302-u4-run003/render-narrow-figures.txt):
every one of the eight figures renders at its full intrinsic width inside a <figure> whose
computed overflow-x is auto - fig-U4-1 900px, fig-U4-2 900px, fig-U4-3 880px, fig-U4-4 940px,
fig-U4-5 880px, fig-U4-6 900px, fig-U4-7 920px, fig-U4-8 880px - against a 328px content box. The
visible fraction is 0.37 to 0.39; the rest is reachable only by horizontal scrolling inside the
figure. The figure element carries no tabindex, no role and no aria-label.
This corrects run-002's accessibility record, which states "figures lay out at 328px". They do
not; the page has no horizontal overflow because the figure scrolls, not because the image is
scaled down.
Why it is uncertain rather than blocking: the same unit already treats the five ERQ rubric tables
the other way - tabindex="0", role="region", aria-label "Scrollable table, scroll sideways to see
all columns" - so the inconsistency is real. But nothing in the bound inputs states a rule for
figure scroll containers (specs/content/style-guide.md has no scroll-container clause;
src/components/Figure.tsx is not a bound input in this manifest), and Chromium 149 makes
scrollers keyboard-focusable by default, so my single-browser evidence cannot establish the
WCAG 2.1.1 failure that other engines would show. The instructional meaning is separately
recoverable: all eight alt texts are present and descriptive, and A4 print emulation lays every
figure out whole at 640-760px with no clipping.
PLATFORM DECISION NEEDED: either apply the table treatment to the figure carrier in
src/components/Figure.tsx, or record that scaled-to-fit figures are the intended narrow-viewport
behaviour. This is a component-level question, not a Unit 4 authoring defect, and should not be
pushed back to the unit author.
